facts.text: The name 'Cambrian Park' first appeared in 1950s newspapers, referring to Union and Cambrian school areas, the latter named by ranch hand David Lewis in the 1870s.
The Cambrian Park Plaza was originally built in 1953 at the crossroads of Camden and Union Avenues.
A colorful carousel atop the Plaza’s sign is a designated historical landmark, adding a touch of mid‑century charm.
The We and Our Neighbors clubhouse, built in 1910, is a San Jose Historic Landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Cambrian Park has long been centered around its Plaza, which has housed a mix of local shops and national brands since its opening.
The neighborhood hosts a branch of the San Jose Public Library, offering free community resources and a weekly free newspaper called the Cambrian Resident.
